extra: What you give up without replays

Replays show hesitation: a cursor that hovers, a visitor who reads the same paragraph twice, copy that gets misread. Trace can't see any of that, because it never records a session. What it does see is every click that went nowhere, every error, every form left half done and every step people drop out of, counted across all visitors instead of the few sessions someone had time to watch.

In practice most fixes come from the second list. For the first, five short user interviews tell you more than a thousand replays, and they don't need a recording of anyone.
week1: Compare Trace's top three problems with what your team found in replays. Ship the first one.
week4: Read the verdict on what you shipped. Keep what still earns its place. Most teams keep replays for support.
faq: Can Trace replace FullStory?
For finding and fixing UX problems, often yes. If support watches replays to resolve tickets, keep FullStory for that.
Without replays, how do I know why people struggle?
Trace tells you where and how often: the element, the page, the error and the share of visits. In our demo shop, that is enough to see that 436 visits clicked a photo that isn't a link.
Can a PM use it without a coding agent?
Yes. The dashboard ranks the problems and shows goals and funnels. Each problem is a written task you can hand to a developer.

Can I use it without a developer?
You need the tag added once. After that the dashboard shows the ranked problems, and each one is a written task you can send to your agency.
Does it work on Shopify checkout?
Not inside it. Shopify only allows sandboxed pixels on its checkout pages, so Trace sees your store up to the checkout button. The checkout itself is not measured yet.
Why are my Trace numbers higher than Hotjar's?
Trace counts visitors who decline cookies too. Ad blockers affect both.

faq: Do I need to re-instrument my events?
No. Clicks, pageviews, forms and errors are automatic. Call trace.track() only for the events that mark a goal.
How accurate is cookieless counting?

A visitor is a hash of address and browser, salted daily. Two people behind one office network with the same browser can look like one, and a returning visitor counts again the next day unless signed in. Funnels and error rates per visit are unaffected.
Can my coding agent read Mixpanel too?
Yes, through Mixpanel's MCP server. The difference is what it gets: Trace hands it ranked problems with evidence, and checks the fix.

Not necessarily. Plausible is excellent for traffic. Add Trace for what happens after people arrive.
Is Trace as private as Plausible?

Both are cookieless and keep no personal data. Trace also records element labels and error messages, so it scrubs them twice. Patterns can't catch a name in a label, so mask those elements with data-trace-mask.
Does a busy site use up events faster?
Yes. Every click is an event, so 100,000 Trace events go further on a small site than on a busy one. Self-hosting has no limit.
